title: Immunotherapy Dosing Schedule Calculator
problem: Allergists must manually calculate and adjust subcutaneous immunotherapy (SCIT) dosing schedules for each patient, accounting for build-up phases, maintenance doses, vial mixing concentrations, and missed-dose adjustments. Errors in dosing can cause anaphylaxis. Each new patient plan takes 15-30 minutes to build, and adjustments for missed appointments add more time.
who: Allergists managing immunotherapy patients in private practice and clinic settings

skill_spec.name: Immunotherapy Dosing Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates SCIT build-up and maintenance dosing schedules with missed-dose adjustment protocols

inputs.name: days_since_last
inputs.label: Days since last injection (for missed dose)

skill_spec.formula_hint: Conventional build-up: start 0.05mL of 1:10000, increase 0.05-0.1mL per visit. Missed dose >7 days at build-up: reduce 25-50%. Missed >28 days at maintenance: reduce to last tolerated build-up dose. Cluster: multiple injections per visit.

example_queries: Patient missed allergy shots for 3 weeks during build-up phase, currently at 0.3mL of 1:100. What dose should I restart at?
Calculate a conventional build-up schedule for dust mite and cat dander immunotherapy starting today
Patient had a large local reaction at 0.4mL maintenance dose. What's the adjusted next dose?

title: Allergy Skin Test Result Interpretation Calculator
problem: Allergists perform 20-80 skin prick tests per patient and must measure wheal/flare sizes, compare to positive/negative controls, grade reactions, and determine clinical significance vs. sensitization. Manual measurement and interpretation is time-consuming and subjective. Inconsistent grading between providers affects treatment decisions and immunotherapy formulations.
who: Allergists and allergy nurses performing and interpreting skin testing in clinic

skill_spec.name: Skin Test Result Interpreter
skill_spec.one_liner: Grades allergy skin test results, calculates wheal-to-control ratios, and determines clinical significance

inputs.name: test_results
inputs.label: Allergen results: name:wheal_mm (comma-separated, e.g., 'Dust mite:8, Cat:5, Grass:3')

outputs.name: graded_results
outputs.label: Graded results (0 to 4+) for each allergen

skill_spec.formula_hint: Positive: wheal >= 3mm above negative control. Grading: 1+ = wheal equals histamine control, 2+ = up to 2x, 3+ = 2-3x, 4+ = >3x with pseudopods. Invalid if positive control <3mm or negative control >3mm. Flag antihistamine interference if controls abnormal.

example_queries: Histamine control 5mm, saline 0mm. Dust mite 8mm, cat 6mm, dog 3mm, grass 2mm, tree 4mm. Grade these results.
Is a 3mm wheal to peanut clinically significant if my histamine control is 4mm?
Patient has positive control of only 2mm - are these skin test results valid?

title: Anaphylaxis Emergency Response Checklist
problem: Anaphylaxis is the highest-liability event in allergy practice. It can occur during immunotherapy injections, food challenges, or drug desensitization. Staff must execute a precise sequence of interventions within minutes. Errors in epinephrine dosing, delayed recognition, or failure to observe post-injection can result in patient death and malpractice claims averaging $1-5M.
who: Allergists and clinical staff administering immunotherapy, oral food challenges, and drug desensitizations

skill_spec.name: Anaphylaxis Emergency Protocol
skill_spec.one_liner: Step-by-step anaphylaxis recognition and treatment checklist with weight-based epinephrine dosing
steps: Step 1: Recognize anaphylaxis symptoms (skin, respiratory, GI, cardiovascular - 2+ organ systems)
Step 2: Call for help, activate office emergency protocol
Step 3: Administer epinephrine IM (anterolateral thigh) - Adult: 0.3-0.5mg (1:1000), Pediatric: 0.01mg/kg max 0.3mg
Step 4: Place patient supine, elevate legs (if not vomiting/dyspneic)
Step 5: Administer supplemental oxygen
Step 6: Establish IV access, normal saline bolus if hypotensive (20mL/kg)
Step 7: Call 911/EMS
Step 8: Monitor vitals every 2-5 minutes
Step 9: Repeat epinephrine every 5-15 minutes if symptoms persist (up to 3 doses)
Step 10: Consider adjunctive therapy: albuterol nebulizer, H1/H2 blockers, corticosteroids
Step 11: Observe minimum 4-6 hours for biphasic reaction (up to 72 hours for severe)
Step 12: Document event, prescribe EpiPen, provide anaphylaxis action plan
Step 13: Report to practice risk management, complete incident report
warnings: WARNING: NEVER delay epinephrine for antihistamines - epinephrine is FIRST-LINE
WARNING: Biphasic reactions occur in up to 20% of cases - do not discharge early
WARNING: Beta-blocker patients may be refractory to epinephrine - consider glucagon 1-5mg IV
WARNING: Pregnant patients - epinephrine is NOT contraindicated in anaphylaxis

example_queries: Patient developing hives and wheezing 20 minutes after allergy shot - what's the protocol?
What's the pediatric epinephrine dose for a 25kg child in anaphylaxis?
Patient on atenolol having anaphylaxis and not responding to epinephrine - what next?

title: Epinephrine Auto-Injector Weight-Based Dosing Calculator
problem: Allergists prescribe epinephrine auto-injectors for every anaphylaxis-risk patient. Determining correct device (EpiPen Jr vs EpiPen vs Auvi-Q dosing), appropriate weight thresholds, and insurance-covered alternatives is a frequent task. Dosing errors in pediatric patients are particularly dangerous. Parents need clear action plans with exact dosing.
who: Allergists managing food allergy, venom allergy, and drug allergy patients across all ages

skill_spec.name: Epinephrine Dosing & Device Selector
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates weight-based epinephrine dosing and recommends appropriate auto-injector device
skill_spec.formula_hint: Standard dose: 0.01mg/kg IM, max 0.5mg adult. EpiPen Jr (0.15mg): 15-30kg. EpiPen (0.3mg): >30kg. Auvi-Q has 0.1mg for 7.5-15kg. Consider 2 devices for patients >30min from ER. Generics available for cost savings.

title: Oral Food Challenge Protocol Checklist
problem: Oral food challenges (OFC) are the gold standard for diagnosing food allergy but carry significant risk of anaphylaxis. Each challenge requires precise dosing escalation, timing intervals, staff readiness, consent documentation, and post-challenge monitoring. Protocols vary by food, patient age, and risk level. Errors in protocol execution create liability and patient safety risks.
who: Allergists performing diagnostic and therapeutic oral food challenges in office settings

skill_spec.name: Oral Food Challenge Protocol
skill_spec.one_liner: Complete oral food challenge preparation, dosing escalation, and monitoring checklist by food type and risk level
steps: Step 1: Review patient eligibility - confirm no recent anaphylaxis, asthma controlled (FEV1 >80%), no beta-blockers, antihistamines held 7 days
Step 2: Obtain written informed consent documenting risks including anaphylaxis
Step 3: Verify emergency equipment: epinephrine, oxygen, IV supplies, suction, crash cart
Step 4: Baseline vitals, lung exam, skin assessment
Step 5: Prepare food portions per protocol (typically 6-7 escalating doses over 2-3 hours)
Step 6: Dose 1 - lip touch, observe 15 minutes
Step 7: Dose 2-6 - escalating doses (e.g., 1mg, 3mg, 10mg, 30mg, 100mg, 300mg, 1000mg protein), observe 15-30 min between doses
Step 8: Monitor for objective signs: urticaria, angioedema, vomiting, wheezing, hypotension
Step 9: If reaction occurs: stop challenge, treat per anaphylaxis protocol, document failing dose
Step 10: If challenge passed: observe 1-2 hours post final dose
Step 11: Document results, update allergy list, provide guidance on food introduction
Step 12: Schedule follow-up, provide written dietary guidance
warnings: WARNING: IV access recommended for high-risk challenges (prior anaphylaxis, low threshold)
WARNING: Never perform OFC on patients with uncontrolled asthma
WARNING: Challenge must be supervised by physician trained in anaphylaxis management
WARNING: Late-phase reactions can occur 4-6 hours post-challenge

example_queries: What's the dosing schedule for a peanut oral food challenge in a 6-year-old?
Patient is on atenolol - can I still do the food challenge?
What pre-challenge labs and criteria do I need to check before an egg OFC?

title: Spirometry (PFT) Result Interpretation Calculator
problem: Allergists perform spirometry regularly for asthma patients but interpreting results requires calculating percent predicted values based on age, height, sex, and ethnicity using GLI-2012 reference equations. Determining obstruction severity, bronchodilator response significance, and tracking trends over time is calculation-intensive. Misinterpretation affects asthma severity classification and treatment decisions.
who: Allergists managing asthma patients who perform in-office spirometry

skill_spec.name: Spirometry Result Interpreter
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates percent predicted values, grades obstruction severity, and assesses bronchodilator response from spirometry data
skill_spec.formula_hint: GLI-2012 reference equations for predicted values. Obstruction: FEV1/FVC < LLN. Severity by FEV1%predicted: Mild >=70%, Moderate 60-69%, Moderately Severe 50-59%, Severe 35-49%, Very Severe <35%. Significant BD response: >=12% AND >=200mL improvement in FEV1.

example_queries: 45-year-old male, 175cm, FEV1 2.8L pre and 3.3L post-bronchodilator, FVC 4.2L. Interpret these PFTs.

Missing deadlines risks loss of board certification, which disqualifies from insurance panels and hospital privileges. Requirements differ between ABAI, ABIM, and state boards.

title: Venom Immunotherapy Dosing and Schedule Calculator
problem: Venom immunotherapy (VIT) for insect sting allergy has specific protocols distinct from aeroallergen immunotherapy. Dosing schedules vary by venom type (honeybee, yellow jacket, wasp, hornet, fire ant), with different maintenance doses and duration recommendations based on reaction severity. Mixed venom formulations add complexity. Guidelines on when to stop VIT depend on patient risk factors.
who: Allergists managing patients with Hymenoptera venom allergy and anaphylaxis history

skill_spec.name: Venom Immunotherapy Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates venom immunotherapy build-up schedules, maintenance doses, and duration recommendations by venom type and risk level

inputs.name: reaction_severity
inputs.label: Sting reaction severity (large local/mild systemic/moderate systemic/severe anaphylaxis)

skill_spec.formula_hint: Standard maintenance: 100mcg per venom. Mixed vespid counts as one. Honeybee separate. Conventional build-up: 16 weeks. Rush: 1-2 days. Duration: minimum 5 years, indefinite if mastocytosis, very severe reaction, or honeybee. Consider 3 years if mild systemic and normal tryptase.

example_queries: Patient had anaphylaxis to yellow jacket and wasp stings - what's the VIT maintenance dose for mixed venom?
Patient has been on honeybee VIT for 5 years with normal tryptase - can we stop?
